title: Sharing styling of `refinementList` items
body:
I feel like in most implementation we do, most of the `refinementList`-type widgets (menu, hierarchical, priceRange) share the same base styling.

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/283419/10815905/3b0abade-7e2f-11e5-95c9-13a13bf4c283.png)![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/283419/10815906/3ee215ee-7e2f-11e5-90bc-5b5a16ac0a3d.png)

^ Here the blue border, bold and grey underline.

With the way themes are currently handled, we have to duplicate this styling for every widget (`ais-menu--item`, `ais-hierarchical-menu--item`, etc).

I see two ways to fix that:

1. Using Sass mixins. We create a base `@refinement-item` for example and we then use it in every widget, allowing us to easily re-use some code. This will help factorize some code, but might make it less readable.
2. We add a `ais-default--item` class to every item, and style this one. This is consistent with how we handle header and footers, but puts all the responsability of defining what is a `refinementList`-like widget and what is not on the library and not on the themes.

I'm unsure which one to chose. Feedbacks welcome.
